categories.name: Phones, messaging and social
categories.tip: Don't delete the app, sign out or reset your phone. None of that fixes a fault at their end, and signing out can leave you locked out until it is repaired.

categories.name: Email, office and teamwork
categories.tip: An outage doesn't normally affect what you have already saved. Carry on with something else and try again later, rather than reinstalling or resetting anything.

categories.name: Tax and government
categories.tip: If a deadline is close, take a screenshot of the error showing the date and time, then try again later.

categories.name: Accounts, payments and banking
categories.tip: Hold off re-keying a payment that failed. Retrying during an outage can sometimes charge a customer twice. Note the sale and try again once the service is back, or use another way to pay.

categories.name: Websites and online shops
categories.tip: Your website's content is safe. Visitors may see errors until the host recovers, and there is nothing to fix at your end.

categories.name: The internet's plumbing
categories.tip: Thousands of unrelated websites and apps run on these. When one fails, lots of things break at once, and it isn't your wifi.

categories.name: AI assistants
categories.tip: Try again in a few minutes. If you're part-way through something, copy your text somewhere safe first.

categories.name: TV, music, games and shopping
categories.tip: Check here before restarting your router or console. If the fault is theirs, nothing at home will fix it.
